title: Pick the line from the literary work that illustrates the claim
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 41 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **41 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 12 Easy, 18 Medium, 11 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage introduces a novel, play, poem, story or older nonfiction book by title and author, makes a claim about a character, narrator or theme, and ends in a colon or a blank.
- The question asks which quotation from the work most effectively illustrates the claim.
- All four choices are quoted lines from the work.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Reduce the claim to its essential descriptors, usually two, such as 'hardworking AND fully devoted' or 'sees others as carefree EVEN WHILE working'.
- 2) Paraphrase each quotation in plain words, ignoring the old-fashioned or poetic phrasing.
- 3) Choose the one that shows every descriptor.
- Stating a related mood is not enough.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You choose a line that has the right emotional tone or vocabulary but shows only half of the claim, for example the character is happy but not working, or working but not devoted.
Sometimes the trap line comes from the right scene but describes something unrelated.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
